sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Structural Drafting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Civil Law (Quebec private law under the Civil Code of Quebec, French civil tradition) overlaid with a Federal common-law public and regulatory framework, including the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and the Criminal Code of Canada
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force since 1 October 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended (FINTRAC framework); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part II.1 (terrorist financing freezing); Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21 (Magnitsky sanctions); Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 10; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, arts. 10.1 et seq. (Quebec significant-control register); Regulation respecting the register of persons having significant control; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2186, 2236–2242 (limited partnership).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport (statutory declaration of identity) for each general partner and each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in jurisdiction of origin; passport issued by national passport authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada is a Convention party since 11 January 2024; Quebec competent authority: Ministere de la Justice du Quebec)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status of the general partner (if a legal person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the general partner's jurisdiction of formation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation / constitutive documents of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the general partner's jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the issuing jurisdiction is not a Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source-of-funds attestation for each limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille where required by the receiving bank or FINTRAC-reporting entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, directors, and UBOs against the consolidated UN Security Council sanctions list, the Canadian Regulations under the United Nations Act, the National Counterterrorism Entity list administered by the RCMP, FINTRAC directives (including the politically exposed persons due diligence regime), and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list for USD-denominated wire and Wise payment rails; enhanced continuous monitoring required whenever a partner is a senior public official or holds a high-ranking political exposure in any jurisdiction, applying the FATF 40 Recommendations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises; online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), the principal registered name of a Quebec enterprise must be in French unless a statutory exception applies; Latin-script transliteration and official French diacritics are recognized; the REQ verifies that the name is not misleading, is distinctive, and contains a mandatory suffix or descriptor indicating limited partnership status, with the French abbreviation 's.e.c.' or the English equivalent 'L.P.' where applicable; bilingual names are permitted only where the French version is the primary registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations issued by the REQ are valid for 90 days and are not renewable; if the reservation is ultimately refused, a new application may be filed with distinguishing elements; an administrative reconsideration may be requested in writing from the Registrar within 30 days of the refusal decision, specifying the distinctiveness and lawful use of the proposed name; upon final administrative refusal, the applicant may institute a judicial appeal before the Cour du Quebec within 30 days of notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally accepted for non-licensed engineering CAD and BIM drafting entities in Quebec provided a physical service address within the province is designated, a registered agent for service of process is maintained, and the registered office is capable of receiving notices; the REQ and Revenu Quebec do not require on-premise staff for a low-risk partnership, but full administrative virtual-office arrangements that cannot receive physical legal process are not permissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 5-10% annual probability); no statutory on-site inspection applies to a non-regulated CAD/BIM outsourcing partnership, but a targeted Revenu Quebec or FINTRAC audit may trigger an unscheduled visit if the business profile changes or tax indicators are triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2261 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 11, 22, 26 and its Regulation (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar), 2050 rue Bleury, Montréal QC
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Registration Statement) filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited partnership under the Civil Code of Québec; contributions are contractual and may be made in money, property, or services, with limited partners restricted in contributing services. No escrow account or capital deposit certification is required at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned General Partner of the Limited Partnership, acting pursuant to the Limited Partnership Agreement dated [●], hereby: (1) approves its capital contribution and the admission of each Limited Partner as set forth in the Agreement; (2) fixes and adopts the registered office of the Partnership at [address], Quebec, and designates the Registraire des entreprises du Québec as the service address required for registration; (3) appoints [name] as gérant/principal manager with authority to open banking accounts, sign tax filings, and represent the Partnership before all administrative authorities; and (4) authorizes the execution of the Déclaration d'immatriculation and any amendment necessary to commence the BIM and civil infrastructure drafting business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name research service (Recherche d'un nom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search through the REQ online portal and obtain an attestation de recherche d'appellation (name search certificate). The proposed legal name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise, and compliant with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) for collective names.
required_dossiers: Resolution of the general partner approving the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit an alternative name or file written representations with REQ within 30 days; a new name search may be lodged at the applicable fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and Limited Partners (private contracting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the contrat de société en commandite in French or English. The agreement must set out capital commitments, profit sharing, management rights of the general partner, restrictions on limited partners participating in management, and the term of the partnership. Notarization is not mandatory unless partnership interests are publicly offered or a partner contributes real property.
required_dossiers: Identification documents (passport) and proof of address of each partner
Certificate of existence or juridical extract for any corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The agreement may be amended by unanimous or majority consent under its terms; if real property is contributed and query arises, re-execute the relevant deed before a Quebec notary prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — 2050 rue Bleury, Montréal QC or online Services en ligne portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Déclaration d'immatriculation for a société de personnes. State the partnership's legal name, establishment (registered office) address, sector of activity (NAICS 541330 / ISIC 7110), identity of each general partner and of the gérant (principal manager), and the fact that it is a limited partnership. Pay the statutory fee of CAD 50 by secure online payment; the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) is created upon approval.
required_dossiers: Attestation de recherche d'appellation (name search certificate)
Copy of the limited partnership agreement (upon REQ request)
Identification and contact details of the general partner and gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a demande de renseignements complémentaires, respond within 15 days through the REQ portal with corrected French drafting or missing documents; failure to respond results in refusal and the declaration must be re-filed with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of enterprise number (NEQ) and certificate of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the attestation d'immatriculation and the official extract of the enterprise. Verify the accuracy of all disclosed information, including legal name, registered office, partners, and activity codes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the extract contains errors, file a déclaration modificative (amendment) with REQ without delay, attaching evidence of the correct facts; effective-dated corrections are available for inaccuracies present at the time of initial filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (Clé / Inforoute) and Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the NEQ with Revenu Québec to activate the GST/HST and QST accounts; export of CAD/BIM services to non-residents is generally zero-rated. If employees will be hired, register for source deductions and establish a payroll account with CRA; the CRA business number is correlated with the NEQ.
required_dossiers: REQ extract and attestation containing the NEQ
Name and address of the gérant
Bank account details for refunds and offsets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business number is not activated or an assessment notice is received, respond within 30 days by filing the relevant return or written submission; a request for retroactive adjustment of the registration effective date may be submitted to Revenu Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance minute book, banking and payment rails execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner / gérant; external counsel and bank compliance officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Canadian business bank account under the exact registered name, adopt a minute book containing the partnership agreement, the first resolution, and the register of partners, and appoint an AML/KYB compliance contact. Finalize wire transfer and Wise payment rail onboarding for client invoicing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, supply the REQ extract, a written organizational chart, and notarized identification; if needed, provide a counsel reference letter confirming the partnership's existence and good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) — no industrial license required for office-based CAD/BIM services; professional engineering acts, if any, remain under the supervision of a member of the Ordre des ingénieurs du Québec (OIQ)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — CAD/BIM production and structural drafting as a back-office support service is not a licensed trade in Quebec; no activity-specific operating permit is required unless the enterprise performs reserved engineering acts without supervision, in which case an OIQ permit would apply

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based service activity; no environmental authorization required under s. 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2); no industrial establishment, no EIA or attestation d'assainissement required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to operations; electronic waste and computer equipment disposal must comply with the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises (CQLR c Q-2, r. 29) — e-waste must be delivered to recognized Quebec recyclers

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Leased office must obtain a municipal fire safety certificate for the occupancy type; compliance with the Building Act (CQLR c B-1.1) for structural and fire-safety load limits; if staff are employed, registration of the establishment with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1), including workplace ergonomics and emergency evacuation planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal GST/HST, Income Tax Act administration, Business Registration Online (BRO) at www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency; Revenu Québec (www.revenuquebec.ca) — Quebec Sales Tax (QST), provincial income tax, QST registration and filing for all registrants with a Quebec establishment; Registraire des entreprises du Québec (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) — mandatory Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) for any partnership carrying on an enterprise in Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Appoint an agent for service of process in Canada if the foreign LP has no place of business in Canada. Step 2: Obtain a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account via CRA Business Registration Online (form RC1 or RC160 for non-resident registrants). Step 3: Register the limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the NEQ (mandatory before carrying on an enterprise in Quebec). Step 4: File the joint GST/HST-QST registration (form LM-1-V) with Revenu Québec to activate the QST number; Quebec administers the federal GST/HST collection for Quebec-based suppliers under the CRA-Revenu Québec collection agreement. Step 5: Registration becomes compulsory in the calendar quarter in which worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in the current or preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold to recover input tax refunds. Step 6: Non-resident LPs must file a partnership information return (TP-600 for Quebec; T5013/Partnership Return if any member is Canadian-resident) and may be required to withhold on distributions to non-resident partners under Part XIII.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax purposes under ITA s. 96: each partner computes its share of income as if the business were carried on directly, and no entity-level income tax is imposed on the LP itself. For GST/HST/QST, however, the partnership is a separate 'person' (ETA s. 248; QSTA) and must register once the small-supplier threshold is exceeded. Territorial scope: Canada taxes each partner on worldwide income if resident, but non-resident partners are taxable only on Canadian-source income allocated from the partnership, subject to tax treaty relief. No income-tax-exempt zones or special tax-free jurisdictions exist within Quebec; the federal income tax and Quebec provincial tax apply concurrently.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box regime; available statutory and administrative elections relevant to a CA_LP include: (i) ETA s. 150 voluntary registration election permitting a small-supplier LP to register early and claim input tax credits; (ii) ETA s. 211 joint venture election permitting a qualifying civil-infrastructure joint venture to be treated as a single person for GST/HST; (iii) ETA s. 227 quick-method election (generally irrelevant for zero-rated exports); (iv) ITA s. 96(9) election to deem a partnership to be a corporation for limited statutory purposes where conditions are met; (v) ITA s. 216 election for non-resident partners to file a Canadian Part I return on Canadian-source income instead of Part XIII withholding; (vi) ITA s. 18.4 excessive interest and financing expenses limitation (EIFEL) calculations for cross-border hybrid partnership debt; (vii) QSTA provisions permitting a non-resident registrant to elect mirror treatment of zero-rated supplies for QST; and (viii) hybrid mismatch recharacterization rules under ITA s. 18.2/18.21 for interest or royalty payments with disproportionate tax treatment in a foreign jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual VAT-type system: federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST at 5% in Quebec, with no provincial HST) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) — statutory QST rate of 9.5% calculated on the GST-inclusive price, producing an effective rate of 9.975%; combined effective headline rate of 14.975%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148(1) and mirror QST threshold; measured on worldwide taxable supplies over the current calendar quarter plus the four preceding calendar quarters; exemption applies to non-residents only if they do not carry on business in Canada, in which case no GST/HST or QST registration is required for zero-rated offshore BIM/CAD services; registration must occur once the threshold is exceeded or when the LP makes taxable supplies in Canada other than zero-rated exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, digital stamping, or mandatory API clearance regime exists in Canada or Quebec as of the current tax law state. Electronic invoicing in PDF/EDI or PEPPOL-compliant formats is accepted where the registrant maintains a complete and verifiable audit trail. Canada has announced a voluntary federal e-invoicing roadmap based on the PEPPOL framework, but no legislation mandates its use. Revenu Québec requires electronic filing of QST returns and certain prescribed electronic remittances for large accounts through its Mon Dossier Entreprise portal; however, zero-rated export invoices for offshore BIM/CAD services do not require pre-clearance, fiscal stamping, or CRA/Revenu Québec approval.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 (and the mirror QSTA rules for Quebec sales tax), a supply of a service to a non-resident person is zero-rated at 0% GST and 0% QST where the supply is not performed in whole or in part in Canada in direct relation to real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or an individual physically present in Canada at the time the service is performed. Offshore BIM/CAD drafting and structural design (ISIC 7110 / NAICS 541330) delivered electronically to a non-resident civil-infrastructure client will qualify for zero-rating provided: (i) the recipient is a non-resident person not registered under ETA s. 241 nor carrying on business in Canada; (ii) the contractual deliverables (digital models, drawings, BIM data) are transmitted electronically outside Canada; and (iii) no Canadian real property, Canadian-situated goods, or services to individuals physically present in Canada are involved. If the CAD/BIM output is used for a Canadian project or the recipient is registered for GST/HST, the supply becomes taxable at 5% GST plus 9.975% QST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed ISIC 7110 services agreement and statement of work identifying the non-resident client, delivery jurisdiction, and clause confirming electronic delivery of BIM/CAD deliverables outside Canada
Commercial invoices marked 'Zero-rated export — ETA Schedule VI Part V s. 7 / QSTA Schedule VII' showing the foreign recipient's name, address, and tax identification number
Electronic-delivery log or cloud/FTP upload certificate evidencing transmission of the drawing files and BIM models to the foreign client outside Canada
Inward remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103, Wire/Wise transaction record, or bank statement showing foreign-currency or CAD settlement originating from the non-resident client

Non-resident status certificate or statutory declaration from the client (foreign TIN/VAT registration certificate) and an internal zero-rating substantiation memo filed with the GST/HST and QST returns

Note: A Canadian Export Declaration (B13A) and bill of lading are not required for pure services exports; such customs documentation would apply only if tangible goods are also shipped, in which case the B13A must be filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES) before departure
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal 4-year limitation period, extended to 10 years where a misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness or wilful default is established. If zero-rating substantiation is deficient, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at 5% GST plus 9.975% QST, with retroactive assessment, prescribed-rate arrears interest, and penalties: (i) late-filing/remittance penalty of 5% of the unremitted net tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months (maximum 17%) under ETA s. 280; (ii) false statements or omissions penalty of CAD 250 to CAD 25,000 per occurrence under ETA s. 285; (iii) tax-evasion penalties of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment on indictment under ETA s. 239, with mirror provisions in the QSTA; (iv) GAAR recharacterization under ETA s. 274; and (v) for the partners, ITA s. 163(2) gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the federal income tax avoided. Revenu Québec applies reciprocal penalties and interest on QST amounts, and the 180-day inward-remittance benchmark is administratively monitored; balances outstanding beyond 180 days may trigger imputed interest on intercompany or partner advances under ITA s. 247 transfer-pricing rules and Part XIII withholding exposure on deemed benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada is Canada's central bank. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration or routine exchange-control authority imposing licensing or surrender requirements on ordinary corporate cross-border payments. The Canada Border Services Agency, FINTRAC, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, the Department of Finance Canada, and financial institutions have separate customs, anti-money-laundering, prudential, sanctions, and reporting roles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is generally convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions, and Canada has no general approval requirement for an LP's ordinary inbound investment, foreign borrowing, foreign-currency conversion, or outbound payment. Transactions remain subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing controls, bank underwriting, tax rules, securities and investment rules where applicable, and reporting obligations. There is no general statutory profit-remittance approval for a Quebec LP. Distributions and allocations must follow the partnership agreement and applicable partnership, solvency, tax, and withholding rules. A non-resident partner's Canadian-source income may be subject to Canadian tax, withholding, information reporting, and treaty procedures; the tax treatment depends on the income, partner, and structure. Obtain Canadian tax advice before distributions, particularly where the LP carries on business in Canada or has non-resident partners.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no general statutory deadline to repatriate export proceeds and no mandatory foreign-currency conversion ratio for receipts from BIM, drafting, or engineering services. Exporters may generally retain receipts in foreign currency or convert them through a financial institution. Canadian export, tax, customs, sanctions, and statistical-reporting obligations may apply depending on the services, customer, destination, and transaction; banks may request contracts, invoices, proof of service, and payment-purpose details.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment-service providers that accept Canadian business customers; provider eligibility, available currencies, and product functionality vary. Wise Business may be considered where the LP and its beneficial owners meet current eligibility and verification requirements, but Wise is not a Canadian deposit-taking bank and its services are not a substitute for a Canadian bank account. Confirm the provider's Canadian regulatory status, safeguarding and deposit-protection treatment, permitted use, transaction limits, and ability to support the LP's ownership and payment corridors. An offshore electronic-money institution does not avoid Canadian AML, sanctions, tax, or bank reporting obligations and may be unable to provide local CAD account details or required Canadian payment services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal statutory requirement for LP partners or directors to attend a bank branch in person. Account-opening methods are bank-specific: some institutions may allow remote or digital onboarding for eligible Canadian entities, while others require an in-person meeting, Canadian address verification, wet signatures, or additional verification for non-resident owners or complex structures. Confirm requirements directly with the selected bank before incorporation or funding. The bank may require identification and verification of the general partner, authorized signers, controlling persons, and beneficial owners, plus partnership and registration records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners, layered ownership, nominee arrangements, or inability to identify ultimate beneficial owners and persons exercising control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the executed limited partnership agreement and amendments; Quebec and, where applicable, extra-provincial registrations; a complete ownership and control chart to natural persons; registers and declarations required by applicable law; certified identity and address evidence for partners, the general partner, controlling persons, and signers; corporate registry extracts and constitutional documents for entity partners; and written explanations of any nominee, trust, or control arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear general-partner authority, inconsistent entity names, or missing authority to open and operate accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide current partnership and general-partner formation records, certificates of status where available, the partnership agreement, general-partner governing documents, resolutions authorizing account opening and payment mandates, signer identification, and a reconciliation of legal names and addresses across tax, registry, contract, and banking records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected receipts or payments inconsistent with an early-stage Quebec engineering/CAD/BIM services business, including large third-party transfers or unrelated high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a business plan, service descriptions, client and supplier lists, signed engagement agreements, statements of work, invoices, deliverables or acceptance records, project budgets, expected transaction volumes and corridors, and an explanation of any third-party payer or beneficiary. Screen counterparties and jurisdictions against applicable Canadian sanctions requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contributions or other funding from unexplained sources, personal accounts, opaque entities, or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide partner contribution records, subscription or funding agreements, bank statements showing source of funds, corporate financial statements and ownership records for contributing entities, source-of-wealth evidence proportionate to risk, and a clear funds-flow diagram linking the remitter to the LP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments described as engineering, infrastructure, or technical services that may involve restricted parties, sanctioned destinations, controlled technical information, or defense-related end use
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide customer and end-user identification, project and end-use descriptions, destination and delivery details, screening results, contract clauses addressing sanctions and export controls, and any required permits or classification analysis under Canadian export-control and sanctions laws. Escalate potential controlled technology or restricted-party issues before performance or payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cash activity, personal-account commingling, unexplained round-dollar transfers, rapid pass-through transactions, or payments lacking a commercial rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adopt documented treasury controls separating LP and personal funds; provide an approved payment matrix, dual-authorization rules, reconciliations, accounting records, invoices and contracts supporting transactions, and a written explanation with evidence for any unusual activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route contributions and loans through an account held in the LP's legal name at a Canadian financial institution or an appropriately regulated provider that accepts the entity and corridor. Use an authenticated SWIFT customer credit transfer or another bank-supported payment rail, with the LP's exact legal name, account details, remitter identity, and a concise, accurate purpose such as partner capital contribution or documented partner loan. No universal Canadian purpose code or foreign-exchange approval code applies to ordinary private-sector funding; follow any fields requested by the remitting or receiving institution. Retain the partnership resolution or agreement, contribution or loan documents, source-of-funds evidence, remittance advice, and bank statements. Do not route capital through personal or unrelated third-party accounts. Confirm intermediary-bank charges, currency conversion terms, and sanctions screening before sending.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Pay overseas subcontractors and vendors from the LP's business account using a bank-supported SWIFT customer credit transfer (commonly documented through MT103 messaging, subject to the bank's current SWIFT format and payment service) or a suitable domestic clearing rail where available. Match each payment to an executed contract, statement of work, invoice, deliverable or acceptance evidence, and approved beneficiary details. For material equipment or goods purchases, consider an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a bank, with compliant shipment and presentation documents; an LC is generally not necessary for routine services. Use documentary collection only where commercially appropriate. Record currency, rate, fees, tax treatment, withholding analysis, and payment purpose; screen beneficiaries, banks, and jurisdictions for sanctions. Apply Canadian non-resident withholding and reporting requirements where applicable, including analysis of service payments, royalties, interest, and other potentially withholding-sensitive amounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards may be used with a bank or eligible counterparty, subject to counterparty onboarding, credit limits, documented commercial exposure, and applicable derivatives, accounting, and reporting requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available for currencies or markets where delivery is restricted or impracticable; availability and enforceability depend on the currency, counterparty, governing documentation, and applicable law. They are not required for ordinary CAD conversion.

Currency swaps may be used for documented funding or cash-flow management, subject to bank credit approval, master documentation, collateral terms, and applicable derivatives and reporting requirements.

Spot foreign-exchange transactions are generally available through banks and eligible providers. Maintain evidence of the underlying exposure and treasury authorization for material transactions; do not assume that every provider offers every instrument or currency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each registration anniversary date; calendar anniversary recalculated after any register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 10 (approx. USD 7); persistent failure may lead to the removal of the partnership from the register, loss of legal-publicity effect, and impaired access to the statutory liability shield for limited partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and Quebec Relevé 15 (mandatory pass-through income allocation filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the 31st day of March immediately following the fiscal year-end of the partnership; if fiscal year aligns with calendar year, due March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under Income Tax Act (Canada) and Taxation Act (Quebec) for late or incomplete filings: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; late-filing penalty for information returns up to CAD 1,000; additional administrative interest and risk of registry enforcement measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for a Quebec limited partnership solely on the basis of entity type; a compulsory audited financial statement requirement arises only if (i) the partnership agreement or unanimous partner consent so stipulates, (ii) a lender or financier imposes an audit covenant, (iii) the partnership is a reporting issuer under securities legislation, or (iv) Revenu Québec/CRA expressly requires audited financial statements in a verification or objection context.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Canada, or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for eligible private partnerships; financial statements prepared under either framework are accepted for tax and regulatory compliance, with necessary tax schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec limited partnerships are not subject to the Quebec Business Corporations Act significant-control register. Beneficial ownership is disclosed through the initial and annual declarations filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, which list all general and limited partners and their contributed amounts. Any transfer of a partnership interest must be recorded in the partnership's internal books and reflected on the next annual declaration. Partners' names appear on the public register, so transfers effectively become public upon filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited and General Partners (containing capital contributions, rights, and transfers)
Minute Book (resolutions of the general partner regarding partnership governance)
Financial Records and Books of Account (under Civil Code of Québec and tax statutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 250 – 600 (approx. USD 185 – 440) per annum for a registered address or commercial agent service in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Statutory audit not required; if contractually or regulatorily demanded, a typical audit for a small professional services partnership ranges from CAD 5,000 – 15,000 (approx. USD 3,700 – 11,000), with review engagements generally CAD 2,500 – 5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5% = 26.5% combined general corporate rate; the LP is fiscally transparent: the corporate general partner pays Part I tax on allocated income (federal T2 + Quebec CO-17).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED investment tax credits: federal 15% refundable (35% for qualifying CCPCs on first CAD 3M), Quebec 30% refundable (SMEs) / 14% (large); Quebec E-Business and multimedia tax credits up to 30% on eligible labour for digital/BIM production; small business deduction can reduce the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income of a resident corporate partner.
